name: Part Identification
description: Ability to correctly identify and name common VEX IQ parts. Progression: 5 basic parts (novice) → 15 common parts (developing) → 30+ parts (proficient) → all parts with functions (advanced).

name: Basic Structural Assembly
description: Building stable structures using beams, plates, and connectors. Progression: connect two beams with guidance → build simple rectangular frame → build stable robot base with bracing → design complex 3D structures.

name: Gear Understanding
description: Knowledge of gear types, ratios, and applications. Progression: understands gears transfer motion → build 2-gear train → understand and calculate gear ratios → design gear trains for specific requirements.

name: Wheel and Drivetrain
description: Building and optimizing robot drive systems. Progression: attach wheels to motors → build functional 4-wheel drive → build stable drivetrain with weight distribution → design advanced drivetrains.

name: Mechanism Design
description: Creating functional mechanisms (claws, lifts, intakes). Progression: understand simple claw → build basic mechanism with help → independently design working mechanism → optimize for speed/strength/reliability.

name: Sensor Integration
description: Mounting and wiring sensors on the robot. Progression: identify sensor types → mount one sensor properly → mount multiple sensors optimally → troubleshoot mounting and interference.

name: Tool Usage and Safety
description: Safe and effective use of VEX IQ building tools. Progression: follow basic safety → use tools with supervision → use all tools independently and safely → teach tool safety to others.

name: Block Programming Basics
description: Fundamental programming concepts using VEXcode IQ blocks. Progression: drag and connect blocks → create simple 3-5 block program → create 10+ block programs → write complex organized programs.

name: Sequential Commands
description: Creating programs where commands execute in order. Progression: understand top-to-bottom execution → sequence 3-4 commands → plan 8+ step sequences → design complex precise sequences.

name: Motor Control
description: Programming motors for movement and manipulation. Progression: make motors spin forward → control direction/speed/duration → coordinate multiple motors precisely → program advanced motor control with feedback.

name: Sensor Programming
description: Using sensor input to make program decisions. Progression: understand sensors provide info → use one sensor in IF-THEN → use multiple sensors with logic → create complex sensor-based behaviors.

name: Conditional Logic
description: Using IF-THEN-ELSE blocks to make decisions. Progression: understand making choices → use basic IF-THEN → use IF-THEN-ELSE and nested conditions → design complex decision trees.

name: Loops and Iteration
description: Using loops to repeat actions efficiently. Progression: understand loops repeat → use simple repeat loop → use repeat/while/until appropriately → optimize programs with loops.

name: Debugging
description: Finding and fixing errors in programs. Progression: recognize when program fails → find simple errors with help → systematically test and fix bugs → debug complex programs and help others.

name: Basic Robot Control
description: Operating the robot with a controller. Progression: move forward/backward → drive all directions and turn → drive smoothly with control → master controller with fluid precise movements.

name: Precision Maneuvering
description: Driving with accuracy and control. Progression: drive without constant collisions → navigate simple obstacles → drive through tight spaces → execute complex precise maneuvers under pressure.

name: Object Manipulation
description: Using robot mechanisms to interact with game elements. Progression: activate mechanisms → pick up and release objects → score objects consistently → manipulate multiple objects efficiently in matches.

name: Active Listening
description: Listening carefully to teammates' ideas and concerns. Progression: let others finish speaking → listen and repeat → ask clarifying questions and build on ideas → synthesize team discussions.

name: Clear Communication
description: Expressing ideas clearly to teammates. Progression: say what you're thinking → explain with some details → explain technical concepts clearly → communicate complex ideas multiple ways.

name: Engineering Documentation
description: Recording design process in engineering notebook. Progression: write date and basic notes → document activities with sketches → create detailed entries with diagrams/analysis → maintain exemplary notebook with insights.
